title: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo

edits.reason: Lesson body elevates the Kijun as the single most-taught component: 'The Kijun-sen is the most important component — it is the backbone of the trend read and the primary trailing stop tool' and the bullet 'Kijun-sen (Baseline)... the most important component; price above = bullish, below = bearish; used as trailing stop'. The chart only draws Kijun as an unlabelled indicator line. A labelled level makes the trailing-stop teaching explicit. yAxis 88 matches the kijun array near the post-twist breakout bars (kijun[9]=87, kijun[10]=88, kijun[11]=90) and sits inside the ~79-116 band. Color pink #ff2e88 matches the chapter's standing Kijun convention (this chapter's own quiz.chart Kijun-sen line and all three ch12 Ichimoku charts draw the Kijun line pink).

notes: REJECTED auditor proposals: (1) introChart Kumo markArea and (2) lessonChart Bearish-Kumo markArea — both redundant; the indicator:"ichimoku" renderer already fills the Kumo cloud between spanA/spanB on every slot, so an explicit markArea would double-draw the same zone (the auditor itself rated both 'low'). (3) quiz.chart Kijun color FIX (pink -> teal) REJECTED — pink is the chapter/module's standing convention for the Kijun baseline LINE: this chapter's quiz.chart already draws it pink and all three Ichimoku charts in sibling ch12 (introChart, quiz.chart) also draw Kijun-sen pink. The bullish 'support' meaning is already carried by the teal revealMarkPoints ('Above Kijun ✓'); recoloring the line would break cross-chapter consistency. The auditor flagged this same risk and said verify against ch12 — ch12 confirms pink is the convention, so leave as-is. ADDED nothing beyond the one accepted Kijun-label markLine; introChart and quiz.chart are concept/decision slots already well annotated (introChart has 4 markPoints incl. 'Kijun = Dynamic Support'; quiz.chart correctly keeps pre-cut context minimal with outcome in revealMarkPoints). Note: green Kumo markArea color rgba(0,180,80,...) is the chapter's established cloud convention (also used in ch12), not the palette teal — intentional and left unchanged.
